text:
irene: quick thread — ran into an awkward leak while building a streaming generator proxy for our edge service. auth refresh can block inside the stream handshake and handler goroutines hang if the HTTP client disconnects. looking for the least-surprising Go SDK ergonomics.

irene: tiny repro in handler form:

```go
func proxy(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    it := sdk.NewGenerator("prod").Stream(ctx, prompt)
    defer it.Close() // currently only unblocks after handshake finishes
    for it.Next() {
        if ctx.Err() != nil {
            return
        }
        fmt.Fprint(w, it.Value())
        w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
    }
    if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("stream error: %v", err) }
}
```

irene: when auth refresh is slow Next() blocks in the handshake path and calling Close() from another goroutine is racy.

kevin: two obvious API directions: 1) make the blocking call accept a ctx (Next(ctx)) so the call is cancellable by request context, or 2) make Close() cancel any in-flight handshake immediately (CloseNow()/Cancel()).

zara: Next(ctx) is my vote for HTTP handlers. it composes with r.Context() and forces callers to think about cancellation rather than relying on deferred Close in early returns. usage becomes:

```go
for it.Next(r.Context()) {
    fmt.Fprint(w, it.Value())
}
```

blake: alternative ideas: provide a token-channel API `Deliver(ctx, ch)` that pushes parts into a channel (nice for backpressure) or a StreamAsReader adapter (io.ReadCloser) for simple streaming. both are useful but orthogonal to handler UX.

kevin: agreed on adapters, but they add surface area. we should first fix the blocking-handshake problem by making the auth refresh path accept context and by providing Next(ctx). that gives immediate benefit to handlers.

irene: test plan: add an httptest.Server + fake auth endpoint that sleeps on refresh. trigger a client disconnect mid-refresh and assert the server handler goroutine exits within N ms. include a helper which times out the test if goroutines leak.

zara: also document sentinel errors. prefer returning context.Canceled from Err() when caller cancelled via ctx, and export ErrStreamCanceled so apps can do equality checks if they prefer. avoid inventing too many new error types.

blake: implementation notes: handshake/token refresh must check ctx on entry, during waits, and on exit so you don't get a race where refresh just finishes after ctx was cancelled and then you deliver an unwanted token. also ensure retry policy respects caller cancellation (do not retry if canceled).

kevin: backwards compatibility: keep Stream(ctx) but add Next(ctx) overload and mark Stream(ctx) as "initialization-only ctx" in docs. include migration snippet in README and a small proxy sample in devex examples.

irene: I'll put up a draft PR with: Next(ctx) change, cancellable auth refresh, ErrStreamCanceled, and a deterministic failing test first so reviewers can see the leak.

ci-bot: Created draft PR #5017: "go: iterator.Next(ctx) + cancellable auth refresh + proxy leak test" — reviewers: @kevin @zara @blake

irene: thanks — attaching the proxy sample and the httptest that closes the client after 50ms while auth sleeps 300ms. if anyone has a concise helper for simulating client disconnects in httptest without spawning extra OS threads drop it here. otherwise i’ll push the prototype.
